rows.behavior: Return a bound logic variable value from a substitution alist keyed by possibly structured variable name, or the original variable if unbound
rows.witness_positive: Bound logic variable retrieves exactly the existing value; unbound variable returns itself
rows.witness_falsifier: Distinguish unbound from binding to empty data, and show a behavior not expressible through D9 WALK plus alist lookup

rows.behavior: Follow transitive bound-variable references until a nonvariable or an unbound variable is reached, preserving the original unbound variable
rows.witness_positive: Substitution chain x→y→a resolves deterministically to a; unbound x remains x
rows.witness_falsifier: D9 WALK/UNIFY or recurrent LOOKUP-SUBST may already express this exact transitive dereference

rows.behavior: Recognize explicit unification failure only for the designated failure atom, not for a nonempty substitution alist
rows.witness_positive: Only the exact designated failure atom is failure; nonempty association list is not
rows.witness_falsifier: An ordinary D3 atom/eq or existing D9 result check can classify identically without introducing a new value

rows.behavior: Unify two dereferenced logic terms recursively, propagating substitutions or explicit failure across compound pairs
rows.witness_positive: Two compatible compound pairs produce substitutions and incompatible atoms return an explicit failure
rows.witness_falsifier: The D9 UNIFY contract already calls this helper; no independent observable semantics demonstrated

rows.behavior: Bind a logic variable to a term when identities differ and occurs-check permits it, otherwise preserve substitution or return failure
rows.witness_positive: Binding a fresh logic variable succeeds but occurs-check rejects x within (f x)
rows.witness_falsifier: D9 UNIFY plus D9 OCCURS-CHECK? already enforce this behavior; show an independently visible semantic distinction

rows.behavior: Evaluate each conjunction condition through an injected goal strategy, branching across every successful intermediate state and collecting final states
rows.witness_positive: Empty conjunction returns exactly singleton list [state], not state nor empty list
rows.witness_falsifier: Compare selected MATCH-CONDITIONS and MAP-GOAL-RESULTS plus D3 COND/D4 LIST/APPEND for full result equivalence

rows.behavior: Continue a conjunction against every intermediate state returned by one condition and concatenate resulting final states in order
rows.witness_positive: A first goal yielding A,B and continuation yielding X,X for A and Y for B returns X,X,Y
rows.witness_falsifier: If D4 APPEND/ordinary mapped recursion derives same order and multiplicity this is a helper, not an additional semantic identity

rows.behavior: Compute free identifiers of sequential let* bindings using each earlier binding only in later initializers and the body
rows.witness_positive: Sequential let* binders affect later initializers and body but not their own initializer
rows.witness_falsifier: Static linter traversal is tooling unless compiler-visible reflection proves an irreducible portable operation

rows.behavior: Compute free identifiers of mutually recursive letrec definitions with all names in scope for all initializers and body
rows.witness_positive: All letrec binder names are in scope in all initializers and body
rows.witness_falsifier: This is an ordinary scoping analysis under ratified binding semantics unless externally observable as new language law
